title: Abba Mari the Exilarch
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He is mentioned in Niddah 67b: his wife was angry with him and did not want to go to immersion, and Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak went to appease her. Seder Olam Zuta says that he was the son of Mar Ukva the Exilarch, and that Rava and Ravina were his sages; Hyman criticizes all its words as fragmentary, corrupt and incomplete. Seder HaDorot cites from the Maharshal’s responsum 6 that Rav Nachman was his son-in-law; Hyman says, with apologies to his holy bones, that the author thought that Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak was the son-in-law of the Patriarch’s house, as is Rashi’s view. Hyman refers to his earlier explanation in the entry Rav Nachman that Rashi’s view too is that Rav Nachman bar Yaakov, not Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak, was the son-in-law of the Patriarch’s house.

notes.text: סע״ז is understood as Seder Olam Zuta. The criticism of that work, genealogy, attribution of the son-in-law confusion and claimed Rashi interpretation remain Hyman’s argument, not a new independent verdict.

The consulted Niddah episode directly names Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak as appeasing the wife. The genealogical, son-in-law and Rashi/Maharshal disagreements remain Hyman’s attributed discussion; the named occurrences do not settle those identities.
